collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager has packed far too much for a three-day walk: unpack it together with a friend, or take all of it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is going on a three-day walk to the far side of the island, and (subject.he/she) has packed. (subject.He/she) has packed a cooking pot, two blankets, a spare pair of sandals, a fishing line, a bag of nuts, a bag of different nuts, a carved turtle for luck, and a small stool. (friend) watches (subject.him/her) try to lift the bundle. It does not leave the ground.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They lay everything out on the floor. "Do you need the stool?" asks (friend). (subject) looks at the stool for a long time. "What if I want to sit down?" "There's the ground." The stool stays behind. So do the second nuts. The carved turtle, after some argument, goes. (subject) sets off the next morning with a bundle (subject.he/she) can actually carry.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) ties the bundle to a pole, hoists it onto (subject.his/her) shoulder, and sets off with tremendous determination. (subject.He/she) is back before lunch. The stool is now somewhere along the path, under a bush, and (subject.he/she) has decided that a three-day walk is really a five-day walk if you are carrying furniture. (subject.He/she) will try again tomorrow, with less.
